reasoning:
These two submissions are functionally identical: each changes exactly one instruction, `ret nz` -> `ret z`, in the eval leaf. Every other line in both diffs is a comment-only edit. So they are genuinely equivalent on the axis that matters most, and I score them equal on correctness_risk; the small splits on minimality and clarity reflect real but minor differences in the comments, and they cancel.

Root cause and whether the change addresses it. Reconstructing the pre-image from the shared context: hl = positional + matVal, then `ld a,b` / `and 8` tests the colour bit and `ret nz` returns the value unnegated for the bit-set side, while the bit-clear side falls through to `ex de,hl` / `ld hl,0` / `or a` / `sbc hl,de`, i.e. hl = -(score). That is a single inverted-polarity conditional return, and it is a sufficient explanation for all three reported symptoms at once. A search maximising a sign-inverted leaf will both refuse free material (capturing the queen or rook makes its own score worse) and print an evaluation whose sign contradicts the material readout. It also explains why the failures reported as still-working are still working: perft, the incremental key/phase/eval-accumulator self-test, legality, castling/e.p./promotion, and forced mate detection are all insensitive to the sign of the leaf value, which is exactly what the report observes. Flipping the branch so the white (Z) side returns positive and the black side is negated restores a coherent white-relative convention at the leaf, and it touches nothing in movegen, display or the accumulator, so the regression surface is essentially nil.

Why 4 rather than 5 on correctness for both. The whole fix rests on one unverifiable-from-the-diff premise: that bit 3 of B is set for black and clear for white. If that polarity claim were wrong, both submissions would be wrong in exactly the same way, since both assert it only in a comment and neither shows any test or repro evidence for the three positions in the report. There is also one loose end neither addresses: the report says a correct build prints about -1786 in position 3 where the buggy build prints 1766. A pure sign flip of the same leaf would give -1766, not -1786. The 20-point gap is most plausibly explained by the corrected search selecting a different move and therefore scoring a different leaf, which is benign, but nothing in either diff confirms that, so a reviewer is left to take it on trust. That residual is identical for both, hence the identical score.

Minimality. Both are as tightly scoped as this fault permits: one instruction. Y edits three contiguous lines (`and 8`, `ret nz`, `ex de,hl`) and nothing else. X edits the same first two plus a fourth, non-adjacent line (`sbc hl,de`) purely to attach a comment, widening the hunk from 9 to 12 lines of context for no functional reason. That is a trivial difference and I am not penalising X for length as such, only noting that Y's hunk is the strictly tighter one, so 5 vs 4.

Clarity. X's comments are the more useful of the two for a reviewer trying to verify the fix, and this is the axis where X wins back what it lost. The defect is precisely a flag-polarity error, so the load-bearing fact a reviewer needs is the mapping of both polarities. X states it in full ("Z = white piece, NZ = black piece") and then annotates the actual negating instruction ("black is negated"). Y gives only half the mapping ("colour bit: 0 = white") and leaves the reader to infer the other branch; its "black -> negate" on `ex de,hl` is well placed at the head of the fall-through block, but it documents less. Hence 5 vs 4.

Merge recommendation: tie. Post-assembly the two builds are byte-identical, so there is no correctness or risk basis for preferring either. If forced to pick one I would take X for the fuller polarity comment, since that comment is what lets the next reader confirm the branch is now the right way round, but that is an editorial preference and not a merge-blocking distinction for Y. What I would actually ask of whichever is merged is the same thing from both: attach the three repro runs from the report showing e6xd5, b3xa1, and a negative score in the bare-king position, and confirm the -1786 vs -1766 discrepancy is a move-choice difference rather than a second defect.

Blinding note: both diffs are the same one-instruction restore differing only in comment placement, which gives me no basis for a theory about authorship or process, and I did not form one. I read only the packet file and no other file in the directory.
